o1.biggest_strength: It spots the two big business truths: Monsoon Dark needs its own track, and subscription win-back must wait until delivery is fixed. It also correctly starts with the 46 to 90 day at-risk group and uses holdouts to measure true lift.
o1.biggest_mistake: The Monsoon Dark message asks people to take a quiz instead of naming a clear closest replacement coffee, which is the main fix this group needs.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Name the exact replacement roast or farm for Monsoon Dark, tidy a few over-specific dates and assumptions, and make the first drafts a little warmer and less operational.

o2.biggest_strength: The writing sounds very close to the brand: warm, simple, not discount-led, and clear about fixing the real reason people left.
o2.biggest_mistake: It does not put the 46 to 90 day customers first as a win-back group, even though they are the cheapest and most urgent people to bring back.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the 46 to 90 day group to the top of the programme, subtract holdouts from the value table, and make the financial model a little more conservative and first-order focused.

reason: I would rather use Output 1 because it follows the shape of the business problem more closely: catch people before they lapse, give Monsoon Dark buyers their own path, and do not restart subscriptions until delivery is fixed. Output 2 is better written, but Output 1 is closer to the plan I would actually run.
